title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with tomatoes and dark‑green vegetables, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs prepared as an omelet or scrambled, combined with fresh tomatoes and dark‑green vegetables (such as spinach, broccoli or kale). A source of fat (oil, butter, olive oil) is added for flavor and energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs provide a complete protein containing all essential amino acids.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic color and boosting antioxidant protection.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a carotenoid whose availability increases with cooking.
Fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E and K found in the vegetables.
The meal is quick to prepare and is often served for breakfast or a light lunch.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs supply the body with complete protein that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and tomatoes provide B12, B2 and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and carotenoids from green vegetables help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Eye health support
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin from leafy greens contribute to healthy vision.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: Added fat increases the bioavailability of fat‑soluble vitamins and carotenoids.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Large portions of eggs can raise cholesterol levels in susceptible people.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked eggs may contain Salmonella; ensure they are fully cooked.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Using a lot of added fat increases the dish’s caloric load.

items.title: Oxalates in green vegetables
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should moderate intake of oxalate‑rich greens like spinach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. In a pan, heat the fat, sauté diced tomatoes and green vegetables until tender, then pour in the egg mixture and cook, stirring, to the desired consistency. Optional: add cheese or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat before serving.
